definition_zh: 共和主义者；共和国的；共和党的
definition_en: a person who supports government by elected representatives, or something relating to a republic
core_image: 胸前别着一枚没有王冠的徽章，主张权力来自公民
scene: 集会上，一位共和主义者举着标语，主张废除君主、由选举产生元首。The republican argued for an elected head of state.
sceneCN: 这里 republican 是「共和主义者」（第 1 个义项：支持共和政体的人）；句意：这位共和主义者主张由选举产生国家元首。

senses.title: A supporter of republican government
senses.definition: a person who believes that a country should be governed by elected representatives rather than a king
senses.definitionCN: 主张国家应由民选代表而不是国王治理的人
senses.example: The republican spoke against the power of the crown.
senses.exampleCN: 这位共和主义者发言反对王权。
senses.why: The ending -an marks a person connected with a republic, so the basic sense is the supporter of that system.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -an 标记与共和国相关的人，所以基本义是这种制度的支持者。

senses.title: Relating to a republic
senses.definition: describing something connected with a republic or its principles
senses.definitionCN: 描述与共和国或其原则相关的事物
senses.example: The country adopted a republican constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家通过了共和国宪法。
senses.why: The same -an ending also forms an adjective, which simply describes what belongs to a republic.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -an 词尾也能构成形容词，直接描述属于共和国的事物。

senses.title: A member of a republican party
senses.definition: a member or supporter of a political party that calls itself Republican
senses.definitionCN: 某个自称共和党的政党的成员或支持者
senses.example: The Republican won the state by a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 这名共和党人以微弱优势赢下了该州。
senses.why: Political parties borrow the word for their names, so the adjective becomes a party label.
senses.whyCN: 政党借用这个词作为名称，于是形容词又变成党派标签。

intro.en: Republican is republic plus the ending -an, which marks a person or an adjective connected with the base word.
intro.cn: republican 是 republic 加词尾 -an，表示与基础词相关的人或形容词。

items.en: The base is res publica, the public thing, a phrase for the shared state.
items.cn: 基础是 res publica（公共之事），指共享的国家。

items.en: Old French republique turns the phrase into the noun republic.
items.cn: 古法语 republique 把这一短语变成名词 republic。

items.en: Middle English republic names a state without a monarch.
items.cn: 中古英语 republic 指不设君主的国家。

items.en: Republican appears for a supporter of that form of government.
items.cn: republican 出现，指这种政体的支持者。

items.en: American and French politics turn the word into a party label.
items.cn: 美国和法国政治把这个词变成党派标签。

items.en: Modern English uses republican for both the believer and the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语中，republican 既指信奉者，也作形容词。

note.en: Republican is the person-and-adjective member of the republic family, and it sits near words for democratic and constitutional politics.
note.cn: republican 是 republic 词族中表示人或形容词的成员，与民主、宪政政治词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a state governed by elected representatives
belief in republican government
a supporter of government by the people

normalIntro.en: Republican is republic plus -an, so the ending tells you it is either a person of that belief or an adjective of that system.
normalIntro.cn: republican 是 republic 加 -an，词尾告诉你它要么指持这种信念的人，要么是这种制度的形容词。

normal.en: Republic plus -an: a person who stands for the public thing.
normal.cn: republic 加 -an：为公共之事站台的人。

normal.en: The capital R version is a party name in American politics.
normal.cn: 大写 R 的版本是美国政治中的党派名称。

normal.en: Republican government is government without a monarch.
normal.cn: republican government 就是不设君主的政府。

normal.en: Compare republic and republicanism: the country and the belief.
normal.cn: 对比 republic 与 republicanism：国家与信念。

normal.en: The ending -an works like the -an in American, naming a person or an adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -an 就像 American 中的 -an，表示人或形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a badge with no crown on it, worn on a plain jacket.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚没有王冠的徽章，别在朴素的夹克上。

abstract.en: Imagine a speaker at a rally pointing at a written constitution.
abstract.cn: 想象集会上的演讲者指着成文宪法。

abstract.en: Think of a ballot box standing where a throne used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象投票箱立在原来放王座的地方。

examples.en: The republican rejected the idea of a hereditary ruler.
examples.cn: 这位共和主义者拒绝世袭统治者的观念。

examples.en: The country wrote a republican constitution after the war.
examples.cn: 战后这个国家制定了共和国宪法。

examples.en: The Republican candidate visited three states in one day.
examples.cn: 这名共和党候选人一天走访了三个州。

dict_mnemonic.text: republic（共和国）+ -an（人／形容词词尾）＝共和主义者或共和国的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: republic（共和国，源自拉丁语 res publica「公共之事」）+ 词尾 -an，表示与共和国相关的人或性质。

sensesIntro.en: The believer comes first, then the adjective for the system, then the party member who borrows the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 先信奉这种制度的人，再是描述制度的形容词，最后是借用这个名称的政党成员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a citizen loyal to the public thing rather than to a crown.
core.cn: 核心意象：忠于公共之事、而非王冠的公民。

branches.en: The supporter of elected government is the central personal sense.
branches.cn: 支持民选政府的人，是核心的「人」的义项。

branches.en: The adjective describes whatever belongs to a republic.
branches.cn: 形容词描述属于共和国的一切。

branches.en: A party member carries the name into electoral politics.
branches.cn: 政党成员把这个名称带入选举政治。

branches.en: The believer and the adjective share the same loyalty to a republic.
branches.cn: 信奉者与形容词共享对共和国的忠诚。

branches.en: The system adjective becomes a party label through political use.
branches.cn: 制度形容词经政治使用变成党派标签。

intro.en: Republican is a transparent English formation from republic plus the ending -an.
intro.cn: republican 是 republic 加词尾 -an 构成的、构词透明的英语词。

latinIntro.en: The base republic goes back to res publica, the public thing, and -an marks a person or adjective connected with it.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 republic 可上溯到 res publica（公共之事），-an 标记与之相关的人或形容词。

republican 由 republic 与 -an 合成。
republicans 在 republican 后加 -s。
republicanism 在 republican 后加 -ism。
词尾 -ism 构成 republicanism。

items.exampleCN: res publica 是 republic 的远源。

items.example: Publica is the adjective inside res publica.
items.exampleCN: publica 是 res publica 中的形容词。

definition_en: the opinion that people have about someone or something, based on past behaviour or quality
core_image: 街坊邻居提起这个名字时形成的共同评价，像一块慢慢磨亮的招牌
scene: 这家小面馆从不打广告，靠街坊口口相传，几十年攒下了好名声。The little restaurant earned its reputation one bowl at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 reputation 是「名声；声誉」（第 1 个义项：人们根据过往表现形成的评价）；句意：这家小馆一碗一碗地赢得好名声。

senses.title: The opinion people have
senses.definition: the general opinion that people have about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人们普遍持有的对某人或某物的看法
senses.example: The school has a reputation for strict teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以教学严格著称。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to think over, so a reputation is the opinion formed after repeated consideration.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「反复思量」，所以名声是经过反复考虑后形成的看法。

senses.title: A good name
senses.definition: the respect and trust that come from being known to behave well
senses.definitionCN: 因表现良好而获得的尊重与信任
senses.example: He built his reputation on honest dealing.
senses.exampleCN: 他以诚信经营建立了声誉。
senses.why: Because people want a good opinion rather than a bad one, the word often carries the positive sense of a good name.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们想要好评价而不是坏评价，这个词常带有「好名声」的正面含义。

senses.title: The state of being known
senses.definition: the state of being well known by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人熟知的状态
senses.example: Her reputation spread far beyond the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她的名声传到了城市之外很远的地方。
senses.why: A widely shared opinion naturally becomes fame, so being known is a further extension of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 被广泛共享的看法自然成为名望，所以「被熟知」是同一想法的进一步延伸。

intro.en: Reputation comes from Latin reputatio, from reputare, to think over, built from re- and putare, to consider.
intro.cn: reputation 来自拉丁语 reputatio，源自动词 reputare（反复思量），由 re- 与 putare（思考、估算）构成。

items.en: Putare means to think, reckon, or judge, and it also gives us compute.
items.cn: putare 意为思考、估算或判断，也是 compute 的来源。

items.en: Reputare adds re-, over again, and means to consider something repeatedly.
items.cn: reputare 加上 re-（反复），意为反复考虑某事。

items.en: Reputatio names the judging and the standing that results from it.
items.cn: reputatio 指评判行为以及由此形成的地位。

items.en: Old French reputation keeps the sense of public estimation.
items.cn: 古法语 reputation 保留「公众评价」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reputation names what people generally think of a person.
items.cn: 中古英语 reputation 指人们对某人的普遍看法。

items.en: Modern English uses it for both good standing and simple fame.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它既指良好声誉，也指单纯的知名度。

note.en: Reputation belongs to a Latin thinking-and-judging family, and it sits close to words for fame and standing.
note.cn: reputation 属于拉丁语「思考与评判」词族，与名望和地位的词相邻。

entries.definition: the opinion generally held about someone
having a good reputation
believed by many people to be something
the state of being known by many people
the reputation a person or company has
a person's rank or status in a group
respect gained through success or importance

normalIntro.en: Reputation contains repute, from Latin putare, to think, so the word is literally what people have thought about you over and over.
normalIntro.cn: reputation 含有 repute，源自拉丁语 putare（思考），所以这个词字面上就是「人们反复思量后对你的看法」。

normal.en: Re- means again, and putare means think: think about someone again and again, and a reputation forms.
normal.cn: re- 表示反复，putare 表示思考：反复想一个人，就形成名声。

normal.en: Have a reputation for is the pattern that follows the word most often.
normal.cn: have a reputation for 是这个词最常见的搭配模式。

normal.en: Build a reputation suggests it takes time and repeated acts.
normal.cn: build a reputation 暗示名声需要时间和反复行动。

normal.en: Damage a reputation is much faster than building one.
normal.cn: damage a reputation 比建立名声快得多。

normal.en: Compare reputable: the adjective means having a good reputation.
normal.cn: 对比 reputable：形容词意为「有好名声的」。

abstract.en: Picture a shop sign polished brighter by every satisfied customer.
abstract.cn: 想象每位满意的顾客都把店招擦得更亮一点。

abstract.en: Imagine neighbours repeating the same story about a person until it sticks.
abstract.cn: 想象邻居反复讲同一个人的故事，直到它固定下来。

abstract.en: Think of a name written in many notebooks across a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写进全城许多本笔记本。

examples.en: The company has a reputation for paying on time.
examples.cn: 这家公司以按时付款著称。

examples.en: One scandal can ruin a lifetime's reputation.
examples.cn: 一场丑闻可能毁掉一生的声誉。

examples.en: She arrived with a reputation as a tough negotiator.
examples.cn: 她来时已以强硬谈判者闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（反复）+ put（思考）＝人们反复思量后形成的看法，即名声；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（反复）+ putare（思考、判断）→ reputare（反复思量）→ reputatio（评价、声望）→ 古法语 reputation → 中古英语 reputation。

sensesIntro.en: An opinion formed by repeated thought comes first, then the good version people want, and finally the wide fame that spreads it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先有反复思考形成的评价，再是人们想要的正面版本，最后是把它传播开来的广泛名望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name polished by what people repeatedly say and think about it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被人们反复谈论和思量，渐渐磨亮。

branches.en: The general opinion is the neutral core sense.
branches.cn: 普遍看法，是中性的核心义项。

branches.en: The opinion becomes a good name when it is positive.
branches.cn: 当评价是正面的，就成为好名声。

branches.en: A widely held opinion spreads into fame and public recognition.
branches.cn: 被广泛持有的看法扩散为名望与公众认可。

branches.en: Neutral opinion and good name differ only in direction.
branches.cn: 中性评价与好名声只在方向上不同。

branches.en: Good standing and wide fame both grow from what others say.
branches.cn: 良好声誉与广泛名望都从他人的言谈中生长出来。

intro.en: Reputation is a Latin noun formed on reputare, with English relatives built from the repute stem.
intro.cn: reputation 是在拉丁动词 reputare 基础上构成的名词，其英语亲属词由 repute 词干派生。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means over again, and putare means to think or judge, so reputare is to think something over.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示反复，putare 表示思考或判断，所以 reputare 就是「反复思量」。

items.exampleCN: reputatio 是 reputation 背后的拉丁名词。

items.example: Reputation keeps the Latin noun shape.
items.exampleCN: reputation 保留了拉丁名词形态。

items.example: Reputable adds -able to the repute stem.
items.exampleCN: reputable 在 repute 词干后加 -able。

items.exampleCN: reputed 在 repute 词干后加 -ed。

definition_en: the act of politely asking for something, or the thing that is asked for
core_image: 一个人轻轻敲门，把写着自己需要的纸条递进去，等待对方点头
scene: 客人把需要更多毛巾的请求写在卡片上，前台很快送来了。Her request for an extra towel was met within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 request 是「请求」（第 1 个义项：礼貌地开口要求某事）；句意：她要一条额外毛巾的请求几分钟内就得到了满足。

senses.title: The act of asking politely
senses.definition: the act of asking for something in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式方式提出要求的行为
senses.example: She made a request for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 她请求多给一些时间。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to seek again, so the core sense is the act of asking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「再次寻求」的动词，所以核心义是「开口要求」这个动作。

senses.title: The thing asked for
senses.definition: the thing that someone asks for
senses.definitionCN: 某人要求得到的东西
senses.example: His request was simple: a quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 他的请求很简单：一间安静的房间。
senses.why: The act of asking easily becomes the name of what is asked for.
senses.whyCN: 「请求」这个动作很容易转指「被请求的东西」。

senses.title: To ask formally
senses.definition: to ask for something in a polite or official way
senses.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式的方式要求某事
senses.example: Guests are requested to keep their voices low.
senses.exampleCN: 请客人保持低声。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the noun's action into grammatical form, with the same polite or official tone.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词所指的动作变成语法形式，礼貌或正式的语气保持不变。

intro.en: Request comes through Old French requeste from Latin requirere, to seek again, from re- and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: request 经古法语 requeste 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），由 re- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire, and it also gives us question.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问，也是 question 的来源。

items.en: Requirere adds re- and means to seek again or ask for something needed.
items.cn: requirere 加上 re-，意为再次寻求或索取所需之物。

items.en: The noun requesta names a formal asking or petition.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语名词 requesta 指正式的请求或请愿。

items.en: Old French requeste carries the noun into English with a polite tone.
items.cn: 古法语 requeste 把这个名词带入英语，并带有礼貌语气。

items.en: Middle English request covers both the asking and the thing asked for.
items.cn: 中古英语 request 既指请求动作，也指所请求之物。

items.en: Modern English uses request as both noun and verb in formal settings.
items.cn: 现代英语中，request 在正式场合兼作名词和动词。

note.en: Request belongs to the seek-and-ask family, and it is close to words for appeals, applications, and demands.
note.cn: request 属于「寻求与询问」词族，与呼吁、申请和要求类词相邻。

entries.definition: to need or demand something
something that is needed or demanded
a person who makes a request
an urgent request for help or support
a formal written request signed by many people
a formal request for a job or place
a strong request that is hard to refuse

normalIntro.en: Request contains quest, the seeking root of question, so the memory picture is going out to seek something and asking politely for it.
normalIntro.cn: request 含有 quest 这个「寻求」词根，也见于 question，记忆画面是出去寻求并礼貌地开口。

normal.en: Re- means again, and quest means seek: seek again by asking.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，quest 表示寻求：通过开口再次寻求。

normal.en: Make a request is the standard phrase for the act.
normal.cn: make a request 是表示这个动作的标准搭配。

normal.en: On request means it will be given as soon as someone asks.
normal.cn: on request 意为「一经请求就提供」。

normal.en: At the request of marks who asked for it.
normal.cn: at the request of 标出是谁提出的请求。

normal.en: Compare require: to require is stronger and means need or demand.
normal.cn: 对比 require：语气更强，意为需要或要求。

abstract.en: Picture a note slipped under a hotel room door asking for towels.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条从酒店房门下塞进去，要求毛巾。

abstract.en: Imagine a raised hand in a quiet room waiting to be called on.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里举起一只手，等待被点到。

abstract.en: Think of a form filled out and handed across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象填好的表格被递过柜台。

examples.en: The manager granted her request for leave.
examples.cn: 经理批准了她的休假请求。

examples.en: All requests must be sent in writing.
examples.cn: 所有请求都必须以书面形式提交。

examples.en: Visitors are requested to sign in at the desk.
examples.cn: 请访客在前台登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ quest（寻求）＝再次开口寻求，即请求；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ quaerere（寻求、询问）→ requirere（再次寻求）→ 中世纪拉丁语 requesta → 古法语 requeste → 中古英语 request。

sensesIntro.en: The polite act of asking comes first, then the thing asked for, and the verb reuses the same shape for formal asking.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是礼貌开口的动作，再是被请求之物，动词则沿用同一形态表示正式请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a polite note passed to someone who can grant what it asks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张礼貌的纸条递给有能力答应请求的人。

branches.en: The act of asking is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 开口请求的动作，是核心名词义项。

branches.en: The content of the asking becomes the thing requested.
branches.cn: 询问的内容成为「被请求之物」。

branches.en: The verb repeats the same act in a formal setting.
branches.cn: 动词在正式场合重复同一个动作。

branches.en: Act and object are two sides of one polite exchange.
branches.cn: 动作与对象是一次礼貌往来中的两面。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in grammar, not in the asking.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只在语法上不同，请求本身相同。

intro.en: Request is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin prefix and the seeking root quaerere.
intro.cn: request 是法语形态的名词，建立在拉丁前缀与「寻求」词根 quaerere 之上。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and quaerere means to seek or ask, so requirere is to seek again.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，quaerere 表示寻求或询问，所以 requirere 就是「再次寻求」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 request 与 require 开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of request and question.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 request 与 question 的词根。

items.example: Requirere supplies the stem of request.
items.exampleCN: requirere 提供 request 的词干。
requesta 在法语中变成 requeste。
request 经法语进入英语。
requester 在 request 后加 -er。
requested 在 request 后加 -ed。
词尾 -er 构成 requester。

definition_en: to need something, or to demand it as a rule or condition
core_image: 一张任务清单上，某些条件被画了红圈，缺一项就无法开工
scene: 这份工作需要耐心和稳定的手，体检合格是硬性条件。The job requires patience and careful hands.
sceneCN: 这里 require 是「需要」（第 1 个义项：某事成功所不可缺少的条件）；句意：这份工作需要耐心和一双稳当的手。

senses.title: To need something
senses.definition: to need something in order to happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 为了发生或成功而不可缺少某物
senses.example: This plant requires plenty of sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物需要充足的阳光。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek again, and a need is something the situation keeps seeking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「再次寻求」，而「需要」正是情境不断寻求的东西。

senses.title: To demand by rule
senses.definition: to officially demand something as a rule or condition
senses.definitionCN: 以规则或条件的形式正式要求某事
senses.example: The law requires drivers to carry a licence.
senses.exampleCN: 法律要求司机携带驾照。
senses.why: An authority can turn a need into an obligation, which gives the word its demanding sense.
senses.whyCN: 权威可以把「需要」变成义务，于是这个词带上了强制要求的意味。

senses.title: To make necessary
senses.definition: to make something necessary as a result or consequence
senses.definitionCN: 作为结果或后果使某事成为必要
senses.example: The repair will require closing the road.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修将需要封闭道路。
senses.why: If a condition cannot be met without an action, the condition effectively requires the action.
senses.whyCN: 如果缺少某个行动就无法满足条件，这个条件实际上就「要求」了该行动。

intro.en: Require comes from Latin requirere, to seek again, built from re- and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: require 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），由 re- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Requirere adds re- and means to look for something, especially something missing.
items.cn: requirere 加上 re-，意为寻找某物，尤指缺失之物。

items.en: The verb develops the sense of needing what is sought.
items.cn: 该动词发展出「需要所寻之物」的意思。

items.en: Old French requerre carries the demand sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 requerre 把「要求」义带入英语。

items.en: Middle English require covers need, demand, and obligation.
items.cn: 中古英语 require 涵盖需要、要求和义务。

items.en: Modern English uses it for rules, conditions, and logical consequences.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示规则、条件和逻辑后果。

note.en: Require shares its seeking root with request, and its family includes the noun for a condition and the word for something indispensable.
note.cn: require 与 request 共享「寻求」词根，其词族包括表示条件的名词和表示不可或缺之物的词。

entries.definition: something that is needed or demanded
necessary for a particular purpose
an official demand for supplies or property
to have to have something in order to manage
to ask for something firmly or officially
to make something necessary
to need or deserve a particular action

normalIntro.en: Require and request share the quest root, but require is stronger: it names a need that must be met.
normalIntro.cn: require 与 request 共享 quest 词根，但 require 语气更强：它指向必须被满足的需要。

normal.en: Re- means again, and quire sounds like quest: keep seeking until the need is met.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，quire 听起来像 quest：一直寻求，直到需要被满足。

normal.en: Require attention means attention is not optional.
normal.cn: require attention 意为关注不是可选项。

normal.en: Require sb to do is the pattern for rules that force an action.
normal.cn: require sb to do 是强制行动的规则句型。

normal.en: As required is the phrase for doing something when a rule says so.
normal.cn: as required 意为「按规则要求去做」。

normal.en: Compare request and require: asking politely versus demanding by need or rule.
normal.cn: 对比 request 与 require：礼貌询问与因需要或规则而要求。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist with red circles around the items that cannot be skipped.
abstract.cn: 想象清单上几个不能跳过的项目被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that will not open until three conditions are met.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，必须满足三个条件才会打开。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe that fails if one ingredient is missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱，少一样材料就会失败。

examples.en: The job requires strong communication skills.
examples.cn: 这份工作需要很强的沟通能力。

examples.en: All passengers are required to show a ticket.
examples.cn: 所有乘客都被要求出示车票。

examples.en: The change will require more time than we expected.
examples.cn: 这项改动将需要比我们预期更多的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ quire（寻求）＝不断寻求、必须有，即需要或要求；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ quaerere（寻求）→ requirere（寻找、索取）→ 古法语 requerre → 中古英语 require。

sensesIntro.en: A need comes first, then a rule that turns the need into an obligation, then the consequence that makes an action necessary.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是需要，再是把需要变成义务的规则，最后是使某个行动成为必要的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a condition circled in red that must be met before anything proceeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：被红笔圈出的条件，不满足就无法继续。

branches.en: The plain need is the basic sense of the verb.
branches.cn: 朴素的需要，是动词的基本义项。

branches.en: A rule turns the need into an official demand.
branches.cn: 规则把需要变成正式要求。

branches.en: A consequence can make an action necessary.
branches.cn: 后果可以使某个行动成为必要。

branches.en: Need and demand both point to something that cannot be skipped.
branches.cn: 需要与要求都指向不可跳过之物。

branches.en: Rules and consequences both force the next step.
branches.cn: 规则与后果都强制下一步行动。

intro.en: Require is a Latin verb formed from a prefix and the seeking root quaerere.
intro.cn: require 是由前缀与「寻求」词根 quaerere 构成的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and quaerere means to seek, so requirere is to seek something out.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，quaerere 表示寻求，所以 requirere 就是「把某物找出来」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 require 与 request 开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of require.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 require 的词根。

items.example: Requirere is the Latin source of require.
items.exampleCN: requirere 是 require 的拉丁来源。
require 经法语进入英语。
requirement 在 require 后加 -ment。
requisite 共享拉丁词干。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 requirement。
词尾 -ite 构成 requisite。

definition_en: something that is needed or officially demanded before something else can happen
core_image: 入学通知书背后列着一串必须满足的条件，逐条打钩才能注册
scene: 报名表背面列着语言成绩、体检证明等多项要求，缺一项就无法注册。The entrance requirement includes a health certificate.
sceneCN: 这里 requirement 是「要求；必要条件」（第 1 个义项：必须满足的条件）；句意：入学要求包括一份健康证明。

senses.title: Something that is needed
senses.definition: a thing that is necessary for something to happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或达成所必需的东西
senses.example: A good camera is a basic requirement for the course.
senses.exampleCN: 一台好相机是这门课程的基本要求。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb require points to: the need that must be met.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指 require 所指向的东西：必须被满足的需要。

senses.title: An official rule or demand
senses.definition: an official condition set by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威机构设定的正式条件
senses.example: The building meets all safety requirements.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑符合所有安全规定。
senses.why: When a need is written into a rule, it becomes a requirement in the official sense.
senses.whyCN: 当需要被写进规则，它就成为正式意义上的「要求」。

senses.title: The act of requiring
senses.definition: the act of demanding something formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出要求的动作
senses.example: The requirement of a deposit surprised the tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 要求交押金让租客们吃了一惊。
senses.why: The -ment ending can still name the action itself, not only its content.
senses.whyCN: -ment 词尾仍可指动作本身，而不只是动作的内容。

intro.en: Requirement is require plus the noun ending -ment, naming a needed condition or the act of demanding it.
intro.cn: requirement 是 require 加名词词尾 -ment，指必需的条件或提出要求的动作。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, and requirere means to seek again.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求，requirere 意为再次寻求。

items.en: Old French requerre brings the demand sense into English require.
items.cn: 古法语 requerre 把「要求」义带进英语 require。

items.en: Middle English require covers need and obligation.
items.cn: 中古英语 require 涵盖需要与义务。

items.en: The noun requirement appears for a condition that must be met.
items.cn: 名词 requirement 出现，指必须满足的条件。

items.en: Education and engineering spread requirements in rules and specifications.
items.cn: 教育与工程使 requirements 广泛用于规则和规格说明。

items.en: Modern English uses it for entry rules, legal conditions, and design needs.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示入学规则、法律条件和设计需求。

note.en: Requirement is the noun of require, and it is close to words for conditions that must be satisfied.
note.cn: requirement 是 require 的名词，与表示必须满足的条件的词相邻。

something that is needed

a detailed description of what is required

normalIntro.en: Requirement is require plus -ment, so it is the thing a need or rule requires you to have.
normalIntro.cn: requirement 是 require 加 -ment，指需要或规则要求你具备的东西。

normal.en: Require plus -ment: the condition that must be met.
normal.cn: require 加 -ment：必须被满足的条件。

normal.en: Meet the requirements is the phrase for satisfying every condition.
normal.cn: meet the requirements 意为满足所有条件。

normal.en: Entry requirements are what a school asks for before you can join.
normal.cn: entry requirements 是学校在你入学前提出的条件。

normal.en: A legal requirement is a condition written into law.
normal.cn: legal requirement 是写进法律的条件。

normal.en: The minimum requirement is the lowest condition still accepted.
normal.cn: minimum requirement 是仍被接受的最低条件。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist on the back of an admission letter, each box waiting for a tick.
abstract.cn: 想象入学通知书背面有一张清单，每个方框都等着打钩。

abstract.en: Imagine a doorway with a height bar that everyone must pass under.
abstract.cn: 想象门口有一根横杆，所有人都必须从下面通过。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe card listing what must be in the kitchen first.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，先列出厨房里必须准备好的东西。

examples.en: The job has three basic requirements.
examples.cn: 这份工作有三项基本要求。

examples.en: All new buildings must meet fire safety requirements.
examples.cn: 所有新建筑都必须符合消防安全规定。

examples.en: Experience is a requirement for this position.
examples.cn: 经验是这个职位的必备条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: require（需要、要求）+ -ment（名词词尾）＝要求或必要条件；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: require（需要、要求，源自拉丁语 requirere「再次寻求」）+ 名词词尾 -ment，指必须满足的条件或提出要求的行为。

sensesIntro.en: A needed thing comes first, then the official rule that demands it, then the act of demanding itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是必需之物，再是要求它的正式规则，最后是提出要求的行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a condition that must be ticked before the next step is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：必须打钩才能进入下一步的条件。

branches.en: The necessary thing is the basic sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 必需之物，是这个名词的基本义项。

branches.en: An official rule turns a need into a written condition.
branches.cn: 正式规则把需要变成书面条件。

branches.en: The noun can still name the act of demanding.
branches.cn: 这个名词仍可指提出要求的动作。

branches.en: Personal needs and official rules both set a bar to clear.
branches.cn: 个人需要与官方规则都设下一道必须跨过的门槛。

branches.en: The written rule and the act of demanding it are two sides of one condition.
branches.cn: 书面规则与提出要求的动作，是同一个条件的两面。

intro.en: Requirement is a transparent English noun: require plus the ending -ment.
intro.cn: requirement 是构词透明的英语名词：require 加词尾 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The base require comes from Latin requirere, to seek again, and -ment marks the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 require 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），-ment 标记动作或其结果。

items.exampleCN: require 是 requirement 的基础词。

requirement 由 require 与 -ment 合成。

items.exampleCN: requisite 共享拉丁「寻求」词根。

re- 出现在 require 词干开头。
